ranking.name: Water leaving the land (evapotranspiration)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water leaving the land (evapotranspiration) in East China changed by +0.061 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval +0.049 to +0.072), which is statistically significant (p < 0.001). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is an increase of about 0.150 mm/day.

ranking.name: Air temperature near the ground
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, air temperature near the ground in East China changed by +0.229 °C per decade (95% confidence interval +0.144 to +0.316), which is statistically significant (p < 0.001). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is an increase of about 0.566 °C.

ranking.name: Water in the topsoil
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water in the topsoil in East China shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.14): the estimate is +0.13 kg/m² per decade (95% confidence interval −0.04 to +0.31). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.

ranking.name: Rain and snow (precipitation)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, rain and snow (precipitation) in East China shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.16): the estimate is −0.041 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.099 to +0.015). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.

ranking.name: Water running off the surface
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water running off the surface in East China shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.81): the estimate is +0.0008 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.0057 to +0.0069). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.
